title: Check lint: flag an entry whose text names a second command or an output claim that belongs to another command, such as `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork runs only the backticked command of a Check entry and applies the entry's expectation ("prints nothing", "exits 0") to that command. Spec drafts often join several commands in one entry. The expectation of a later command then lands on the first one:
- S598 (run ork-20261125-232714-f9a7) went red in round 3 on "- `go test ./...` exits 0, go vet ./... prints nothing, and gofmt -l . prints nothing." `go test` passed, but ork applied "must print nothing" to it.
- The S606 and S622 drafts on 2026-11-27 had "- `go vet ./...` reports nothing, and gofmt -l /home/... prints nothing." and "- `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing; gofmt -l ... prints nothing.". Both were fixed by hand before the start.

Owner decision (adj 628, `spec.check-second-command`, "Known commands", 2026-11-27): flag a clause-leading word from a fixed list (go, gofmt, git, slicer, adj, ork), after `,`, `;`, `and`, `or` or `.`, followed by an argument, in a Check entry's text outside the backticks. The finding names that command. All of ork's Check-entry lints go through `checkCommandWarnings`, so this one gets the same three places as S563's lint (`run.start` and `wave.start` refuse, the spec check holds the item, a drafted Check section gets a problem) with no new plumbing. Each command then gets its own entry.

Owner decision, 2026-11-27 (adj 628): known commands list (go, gofmt, git, slicer, adj, ork).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsFlagsASecondCommandOutsideTheBackticks in `internal/engine/brief_test.go`: it calls `SliceCheckCommandWarnings` with a Check body built from entries (empty Files). Each entry's warnings must equal the exact text `Check entry "FIRST": text outside the backticks names a second command "NAME ARG"; put each command in its own backticked entry`, with one warning per second command, in text order. Cases:
  - "- `go test ./...` exits 0, go vet ./... prints nothing, and gofmt -l . prints nothing." gives two warnings, `"go vet"` then `"gofmt -l"` (the S598 entry).
  - "- `go vet ./...` reports nothing, and gofmt -l /home/x prints nothing." gives `"gofmt -l"` (S606).
  - "- `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing; gofmt -l . prints nothing." gives `"go vet"` and `"gofmt -l"` (S622).
  - One case each for `. ` (sentence end), `or`, and the names git, slicer, adj and ork after a clause break (for example "`go test ./...` passes, slicer check --root X exits 0" gives `"slicer check"`).
  - "- `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing" where the entry holds two backticked commands gives one warning, not one for each command.
- TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsAllowsProseOutsideTheBackticks in `internal/engine/brief_test.go`: none of these produce a warning (a body whose commands are all runnable, `go` and `gofmt` being on PATH):
  - "- `go test ./...` exits 0 and lists each new test as PASS."
  - "- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing."
  - "- `go test ./... && go vet ./...`" (a chain inside the backticks).
  - "- `go test ./...` exits 0, then go." (a listed word with no argument).
  - "- `go test ./...` passes when run with go vet clean" (a listed word not at a clause start).
  - "- `go test ./...` exits 0 and Go vet is clean" (a capitalised word).
  - "- HUMAN CHECK: `go test ./...` passes, go vet ./... prints nothing".
  - "- [AFTER LAND] `go test ./...`, go vet ./...".
  - An "Acceptance criteria:" block with such prose followed by "Commands:" and a clean entry.
  - An entry with no backticks, "- go test ./... passes, go vet ./... prints nothing".
- TestCheckDraftCheckFlagsASecondCommandOutsideTheBackticks in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go`: for a changed Check section "- `go test ./...` exits 0, go vet ./... prints nothing", `CheckDraftCheck` returns one `SpecDraftProblem{Section: "Check", Message: ...}` with the exact warning text above. The same commands as separate entries ("- `go test ./...` exits 0", "- `go vet ./...` prints nothing") give no problem. An unchanged Check section gives none.
- TestSpecCheckHoldsACheckEntryThatNamesASecondCommand in `internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`: S1's Check is "- `go test ./...` exits 0, go vet ./... prints nothing". `rig.check(t, "S1", "S2")` gives S1 Ready false, no questions and exactly one finding that contains `"go vet"`. S2 stays ready, no role request mentions the S1 entry, and `d.runs.specs` has no S1 result. After the Check is split into two entries, S1 is ready on the next check.
- TestRunStartRefusesACheckEntryThatNamesASecondCommand in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: with the same S1 Check, `launchPlan` returns one warning, and `MethodRunStart` is refused with `CodeRefused`. The message contains "S1", "go vet", "edit the Check section" and "start again", and no run is created. After the Check is split into two entries, the start returns a run record.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests above and see each one red. They go in the four test files named under Files.
2. In `internal/engine/brief.go`, add a field `outside string` to `sliceCheckCommand`. It holds the entry's text outside the backticks.
3. In `checkBodyCommands`, build `outside` for each entry: join the even-indexed parts of `strings.Split(entry, "`")` with a single space. Set it only on the first command of that entry and leave it empty on the others, so an entry with two backticked commands warns once. `checkRows` and `checkRunByOrk` build `sliceCheckCommand` values without it, so they are unaffected.
4. Add `secondCommands(outside string) []string` near `checkBodyCommands`. It splits the text with `strings.Fields`. A clause starts after a word that ends in `,` or `;`, or that ends in `.` right after a letter or digit (so `.`, `..` and `./...` end no clause), and after the words `and` and `or`. The first word of the text is not a clause start. When the word at a clause start equals exactly one of `go`, `gofmt`, `git`, `slicer`, `adj` or `ork` (case-sensitive, no trailing punctuation) and another word follows in the text, return that word and the next word with trailing `,;.` trimmed, joined by a space (adj 628, `spec.check-second-command`).
5. In `checkCommandWarnings`, at the top of the loop over entries, append one warning for each result of `secondCommands(entry.outside)`: `Check entry %q: text outside the backticks names a second command %q; put each command in its own backticked entry`, with `entry.command` and the name. Do this before the first-word check, so an entry that also fails that check reports both. `SliceCheckCommandWarnings` and `CheckBodyCommandWarnings` share this function. The spec check, `planRun`/`run.start`/`wave.start` and `CheckDraftCheck` therefore need no change. `checkBodyCommands` already skips HUMAN CHECK entries, after-land entries and acceptance criteria.
6. Docs: in `docs/design.md`, add a sentence to the plan warnings paragraph. A backticked Check entry whose text outside the backticks has a clause-leading go, gofmt, git, slicer, adj or ork followed by an argument warns, naming that command, with the same refusal, spec check finding and draft problem as the other entry warnings (adj 628). In `docs/guide.md` "Writing Check lines", add one sentence: give each command its own backticked entry, because ork applies the entry's wording to the backticked command only.
7. Changelog entry: `slicer changelog add S636 --text "A Check entry whose text names a second command outside the backticks is now flagged by the plan, the spec check and the spec draft."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A Check entry whose text outside the backticks has a clause-leading go, gofmt, git, slicer, adj or ork followed by an argument gets a warning that names that command, once for each such command.
- `run.start` and the affected wave.start member refuse such an entry, the spec check holds the item with a finding, and a drafted Check section gets a problem.
- Prose without a clause-leading listed command, text inside the backticks, HUMAN CHECK entries, after-land entries, acceptance criteria and entries without backticks produce no warning.
- The warning text for a Check entry that is not a command or has a missing path argument is unchanged.

Commands:
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsFlagsASecondCommandOutsideTheBackticks ./internal/engine` exits 0 and runs the test
- `go test -run TestSliceCheckCommandWarningsAllowsProseOutsideTheBackticks ./internal/engine` exits 0 and runs the test
- `go test -run TestCheckDraftCheckFlagsASecondCommandOutsideTheBackticks ./internal/engine` exits 0 and runs the test
- `go test -run TestSpecCheckHoldsACheckEntryThatNamesASecondCommand ./internal/daemon` exits 0 and runs the test
- `go test -run TestRunStartRefusesACheckEntryThatNamesASecondCommand ./internal/daemon` exits 0 and runs the test
- `go test ./...` exits 0
- `go vet ./...` exits 0
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing
- `slicer check` exits 0
